title: Reactions of Metals and Non-metals with Oxygen
summary: How metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides, rusting and how to prevent it, and how non-metals burn in oxygen to form non-metal oxides.

notes.text: Most metals react with oxygen to form **metal oxides**. This is called **oxidation**. The general equation is:

notes.caption: Some metals burning in oxygen
rows: Burns with a blinding white flame; forms white powder
Glows and sparks orange; forms black solid
Does not burn; a black layer of copper oxide forms on the surface
Burns with a bright yellow-orange flame

notes.label: Safety
notes.text: Never look directly at burning magnesium; the bright light can damage your eyes. Hold metals with tongs and wear safety glasses.
Metals react with oxygen at different rates. Magnesium and sodium are very reactive; iron and copper react more slowly; gold and platinum hardly react at all, which is why gold jewellery stays shiny.

**Rusting** is the slow oxidation of iron or steel when it is in contact with both **oxygen** and **water**. Rust (hydrated iron oxide) is brown, flaky and weak; it falls off, exposing fresh iron to more rusting. Salt water and acid rain make rusting faster.

notes.title: The rusting experiment
notes.problem: Three iron nails are placed in test tubes: A in tap water open to air; B in boiled water with a layer of oil on top; C in dry air with calcium chloride (a drying agent). Which nail rusts, and why?
steps: A has both water and oxygen: it rusts.
B: boiling removes dissolved air and the oil stops new air dissolving, so there is no oxygen. No rust.
C: calcium chloride removes water vapour, so there is no water. No rust.
notes.answer: Only nail A rusts: both oxygen and water are needed.

items: **Painting**, **oiling** or **greasing** keeps out air and water (gates, bicycle chains).
**Galvanising**: coating iron with zinc (roofs, buckets). Zinc reacts first, protecting the iron even if scratched.
**Alloys** such as stainless steel (iron mixed with chromium and nickel) do not rust.

notes.text: Many non-metals also burn in oxygen to form **non-metal oxides**, which are usually gases.

rows: Glows red; colourless gas forms that turns limewater milky
Burns with a blue flame; choking gas
Burns with a squeaky pop; forms water

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Metal oxides are usually **basic**; non-metal oxides that dissolve in water usually form **acids**. Sulfur dioxide from burning coal dissolves in rain to form **acid rain**, which damages buildings, plants and lakes.
The **limewater test**: carbon dioxide bubbled through clear limewater turns it **milky**. A glowing splint relights in **oxygen**; a lit splint gives a squeaky pop with **hydrogen**.
